fields.System.Title: INB-1 — Advance Shipping Notice
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Capture what a supplier says is coming, so that receiving has something to check the delivery
against.

Scope

In. Creating, viewing, and cancelling ASNs; receiving them automatically from the ERP.

Out. Purchase order management. The ERP owns that; an ASN is its shipping-side shadow.

Design notes

An ASN is an expectation, not a fact. It never creates stock. Only a confirmed receipt does
that. Keeping this distinction clean is what allows over-receipt, short receipt, and blind
receipt to be handled without special cases.

Deduplicate on the supplier reference. The ERP will resend. Without a unique constraint on
(source_system, external_reference), one retried message becomes two ASNs and, eventually,
two receipts.

Blocked products are accepted with a warning, not rejected. The truck is already coming.
Flag the line so receiving routes it to quarantine rather than making the clerk turn it away.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Duplicate ASN from an ERP retry | [doc 09 §3.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Cancelling an ASN that has been partly received | [doc 05 WF 1](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Malformed ERP message dropped silently | [doc 08 §6](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
